notes: Recorded git_commit 42fdf38 is the branch base the measurement actually ran against (the tree is unchanged since); the receipt is committed later, so the recorded commit is deliberately the base and stays an ancestor of main. The grounding slot was reached through a hosted OpenRouter endpoint; a self-hosted run of the same weights would differ in quantization and serving, so these figures are endpoint-specific. Corpus and items: the same assembled corpus the CI local arm builds -- the 96-unit corpus from the repository's tracked fixtures (17 documents) -- was used at --limit 20, giving 25 known-good positives and 44 planted-bad negatives over 69 scored calls. The positives are each unit's own qualifying sentence plus a narrow, meaning-preserving rewrite, so both positive classes are supported by the clause by construction and only the bad-claim arm discriminates; no real-world false-positive rate may be quoted from it. unreadable_answers counts answers the answer parser could not decode, which separates a parsing defect from model hesitation. This is a single sample of a non-deterministic model, not a benchmark. Exact model id: openrouter/meta-llama/llama-3.1-8b-instruct. Gateway cost ledger (cost_logs) for this model on the run date: 73 calls booked at the one-cent floor (73 cents); the four ladder runs totalled 292 calls at the floor (292 cents). The ledger computes max(1, round(cost_usd * 100)) per call (src/openreview_cli/gateway/cost.py), so these cheap ladder models pin at that floor and the totals are call counts, not real money. This receipt is a curated summary of that run's raw harness JSON: the harness wrote ladder-small.json (a scratch path outside the repo) and the curation step that reshaped it into this receipt is not part of the harness. The run's 69 per_label rows are collapsed into the aggregate metrics and the missed_by_generator counts below; no per-row content is carried.
